newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan studying ways to evacuate stranded nationals.
newsitem.headline: Japan studying ways to evacuate stranded nationals.

text.p: Japan is studying ways of evacuating Japanese nationals stranded near the Angkor Wat religious monument in northern Cambodia, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday.
"We are considering (ways to) pick up those Japanese nationals caught in the most dangerous areas," Hashimoto told reporters.
About 90 Japanese nationals, most of them tourists, are stranded in Siem Reap, where fighting was reported between rival Cambodian factions.
Government spokesman Kaoru Yosano told a news conference that Hashimoto ordered officials to study all possible routes out of Siem Reap, including land, air and sea.
"But at this point no routes are secure," said Yosano, the deputy chief cabinet secretary.

On Monday, top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama said Japan might dispatch special government planes to Phnom Penh to evacuate Japanese nationals and other foreigners, but the plan was not carried out because the airport was closed.
On Tuesday, Thai air force transport planes evacuated hundreds of Thai nationals and other foreigners from Phnom Penh.
The fighting between forces under Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and those loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh claimed the first Japanese victim last weekend.
Takamasa Okajima, an engineer, was critically injured when a stray shell landed in his Phnom Penh home on Saturday. He later died in hospital.
